title: Final Metric Values
description: Output of 09_compute_metrics.py. The SINGLE SOURCE consumed by 10_render_report.py and 11_render_deck.py -- guarantees Rule 4 (Internal Consistency) by construction. The top-level object contains EXACTLY 13 keys: the reserved `_metadata` envelope plus the twelve metric keys m1..m12. The underscore prefix on `_metadata` distinguishes it lexically from the metric keys and signals that it carries renderer/provenance metadata rather than a measured value. `additionalProperties: false` enforces the user-prompt constraint 'MUST NOT add metrics beyond the 12 specified'. Each metric carries confidence, provenance, baseline plus either two-phase (post_introduction) or three-phase (ramp_up + steady_state) breakdowns.

metadata.description: Top-level envelope carrying the renderer/provenance metadata for the metrics.json file. Distinct from per-metric `provenance` blocks because the metadata here describes the document as a whole rather than any single metric. Read by both `10_render_report.py` and `11_render_deck.py` to populate the Executive Summary timestamps and the Reproducibility Appendix preamble. The inflection_date_utc field is the canonical phase-partition key per AAP §0.5.6; making it required at the linchpin artifact mechanically satisfies the Rule-4 Internal Consistency contract (the renderer's phase decomposition reads this field, not any raw artifact).

schema_version.description: SemVer string identifying the metrics.json schema version this document conforms to (e.g., '1.0.0'). Renderers MUST refuse to render a document whose schema_version they do not understand.

run_id.description: Per-run UUID4 correlation ID propagated from `00_environment.sh` via the `BLITZY_RUN_ID` environment variable. Joins every log line, every raw artifact, and the final report so a reviewer can trace any number back to the exact run that produced it (Rule 1: Data Provenance).

extraction_timestamp.description: Wall-clock UTC timestamp captured at the moment `09_compute_metrics.py` wrote this file. Distinct from the per-source `fetched_at` timestamps that live in raw artifacts. Strict ISO-8601 Z-form (no fractional seconds, no offset) for renderer consistency.

generated_by.description: Script identifier that produced this file. Always 'scripts/09_compute_metrics.py' in the current pipeline; surfaced as a field so future replacements of the compute step are explicit in the artifact rather than implicit by convention.

inflection_date_utc.description: Canonical AI-introduction inflection point. Module-scope constant per AAP §0.5.6: identical across inflection.json#date_utc, metrics.json#_metadata.inflection_date_utc, per_engineer.json#_metadata.inflection_date_utc, and pulls.json#_metadata.inflection_date_utc. Required at the linchpin so the renderer reads the phase-partition key from the single source of truth (Rule 4 Internal Consistency, AAP §0.5.6).

source_artifact_hashes.description: Optional map from source-artifact filename (relative to data/, e.g., 'pulls.json', 'commits.csv') to its SHA-256 hex digest captured at the moment `09_compute_metrics.py` read it. Lets the verifier confirm that the rendered report was derived from the exact data artifacts present at compute time. Empty object permitted when hashes were not captured.

rudder_server_head_sha.description: Optional 40-character SHA-1 hex of the analyzed repository's HEAD at the moment of extraction. Aids cross-referencing the report against the exact commit it describes.

rudder_server_repo_slug.description: Optional 'owner/repo' slug of the analyzed repository (e.g., 'Blitzy-Sandbox/blitzy-RudderStack'). Surfaced in the report header so a reviewer who sees the rendered document knows which fork it describes.

ramp_up_steady_state_split_applied.description: Whether the after-period was split into Ramp-Up (first 90 days post-introduction) and Steady State (90+ days post-introduction) phases per AAP §0.5.6. When false, the fallback Baseline vs Post-Introduction decomposition was applied because fewer than 90 days of post-introduction data existed at extraction time. Recorded here so renderers consume the phase-decomposition flag from the single source of truth (Rule 4 Internal Consistency) and the report's Methodology section can cross-reference `decision-log.md` DL-006 with one lookup. Mirror of `inflection.json#ramp_up_steady_state_split_applied`.

ramp_up_steady_state_split_applied_reaso.description: Free-text justification for the value of `ramp_up_steady_state_split_applied`. When the split was NOT applied, this field contains the post-introduction duration in days and references AAP §0.5.6 and `decision-log.md` DL-006. When the split WAS applied, this field documents the inflection date and the post-introduction duration that exceeded the 90-day threshold.

ramp_up_steady_state_threshold_days.description: The number of days post-introduction at which Ramp-Up transitions to Steady State per AAP §0.5.6. Always 90 in the current contract; surfaced as a schema field so a future change to the threshold is mechanically visible to renderers and reviewers rather than buried in code.

post_introduction_duration_days.description: The number of full days between the inflection point and the analysis-period end. Used by the renderer to label the after-period axis in the Acceleration Curve and to justify the ramp_up_steady_state_split_applied value. Mirror of `inflection.json#post_introduction.duration_days`.

phase_keys_used.description: The set of phase keys that downstream metric rows are guaranteed to populate. When `ramp_up_steady_state_split_applied` is false this is `['baseline', 'post_introduction']`; when true it is `['baseline', 'ramp_up', 'steady_state']`. Renderers MUST iterate this array rather than hardcoding the phase set so the fallback decomposition is honored without code changes.

schema_version_change_note.description: Free-text justification for the latest schema_version bump. Lets a reviewer scan recent CP-remediation changes without diffing the schema file. Required only when schema_version differs from the prior release; permitted but unused otherwise.

windows.description: Count of 2-week windows that fell within this phase. Drives the 'fewer than 4 windows' insufficient-signal rule for Metric 3 (predictability).

requirement_id.description: User-prompt requirement identifier (e.g., 'M1-FlowLoad'). Used by the Traceability Matrix renderer.

extraction_command.description: Authoritative shell or git command that produced the raw data -- must be syntactically valid bash for the Rule 5 (Reproducibility) verify gate.

raw_output_artifact_path.description: Path to the primary raw artifact under data/ that the derivation read from. When the derivation reads from multiple artifacts, this field carries the most authoritative single path AND the additional paths are enumerated in `raw_output_artifact_paths`.

raw_output_artifact_paths.description: Optional explicit array of every raw artifact path the derivation read from. Required for derivations that span multiple artifacts (e.g., M4 reads pulls.json + reviews.json + pull_events.json). When present, EVERY element MUST be a concrete `data/*.{json,csv}` path that exists on disk — the Rule 1 (Data Provenance) verify gate dereferences each path. Use this field instead of a compound `raw_output_artifact_path` string (`'a.json + b.json'`) so the path list is machine-resolvable. The primary path SHOULD also appear as the first element of this array for renderer convenience.

derivation_function.description: Fully-qualified Python function name in 09_compute_metrics.py that produced this metric (e.g., 'compute_m1_flow_load').

value.description: Final headline value for the after period (or post_introduction in two-phase fallback). The literal string 'insufficient_signal' is the only non-numeric value permitted; this satisfies the user-prompt constraint 'MUST NOT fabricate, estimate, or extrapolate'.

after_before_multiplier.description: After/before multiplier (e.g., 4.7). The em-dash '—' string indicates the multiplier is not computable (baseline or after is insufficient_signal or zero).

confidence.description: Per AAP §0.2.4, the data-source-driven confidence tier. 'insufficient' indicates value == 'insufficient_signal'.

caveat.description: Required when confidence == 'low'. Rendered inline with the metric wherever it appears (Rule 3).

boundary_conditions.description: Required when confidence != 'high'. Documents the constraints that lowered confidence (e.g., 'GitHub API unavailable -- fallback to local git').

reason.description: Required when value == 'insufficient_signal'. The reason string used in the Rule-stipulated 'Insufficient signal -- [reason]' rendering.

extraction_strategy.description: Short prose describing how the metric was extracted, for the Methodology section.

semantic_contract.description: Optional named contract identifier documenting which counting unit the metric uses when the live data source is unavailable. Example: 'merge_commit_fallback' for M2 (Flow Velocity) when the GitHub Pulls API is unreachable and the unit is each explicit merge commit on `main`. The contract identifier is referenced by `decision-log.md` and is consumed by renderers and per-engineer breakdowns so the same unit is used uniformly (Rule 4 Internal Consistency).

semantic_contract_note.description: Optional free-text justification accompanying `semantic_contract`. Documents why the fallback unit was chosen and how it relates to the live-data unit; cited by the per-engineer breakdown in per_engineer.json.

per_window.description: Per-2-week-window values for the Acceleration Curve diagram (Rule: no selective omission).

allOf.description: Temporal-phase decomposition: EITHER three-phase (ramp_up + steady_state) OR two-phase (post_introduction). Per AAP §0.5.6 two-phase fallback when fewer than 90 days of post-introduction data exist.
Rule 3 enforcement: caveat REQUIRED when confidence == 'low'.
Confidence transparency: boundary_conditions REQUIRED when confidence != 'high' (covers medium / low / insufficient).
Insufficient-signal rendering: reason REQUIRED when value == 'insufficient_signal'.
